sources.entry: Browser Agent Blueprint - Open-source browser agent prompt modules and synthetic recovery examples for uncertain actions. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: A set of original, copyable browser-agent prompt modules and a local synthetic demo that teach agents to verify saved state and avoid duplicate writes after a lost response.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides 12 plain-text prompt modules covering core execution, authority boundaries, browser pre-call checks, risk levels, retry classes, external memory, lifecycle, evidence, content entry, and social operations. A small Node assembler (no npm dependencies) combines them into six profiles such as minimal, long, content, validation, social, and full, and reports bytes and hash. A browser-only task-profile builder and an interactive lost-reply simulation are also offered. The demo runs a real local browser against a synthetic page and checks save counts, checkpoint resume across processes, and recovery after killed workers or browsers. It also includes a checkpoint-publication kill test and a write-ahead runner that marks uncertain writes as PENDING_REVIEW. Optional Codex-oriented installation of a browser-task-recovery skill is described. The README states the demos are deterministic host-side tests, not LLM behavior benchmarks.
use_cases: prevent a browser agent from clicking Save twice after a timeout
verify a saved draft by reading back persisted state
resume a long browser task from a checkpoint in a new process
assemble a task-specific prompt profile for a browser agent
test how a browser agent recovers from a killed worker or browser
review uncertain writes before any replay
stack: Codex Agent Skill (optional installer via npx skills)
notable: Lost-reply experiment: with agent-browser 0.38.2 five clicks were sent after a dropped reply, versus one click and an outcome_unknown report on 0.41.0 (local, fictional page)
Write-ahead runner persists uncertain observations as PENDING_REVIEW and blocks new writes until a recorded review
Local allowlist rejects an evaluate action before its executor runs (example controller only)
Assembler reports bytes and SHA-256 rather than claiming token savings
Interactive browser-only simulation and task-profile builder need no installation
caveats: The README states this is not a security sandbox or production safety guarantee; local controller is small and fixture-specific
No server-side idempotency or exactly-once delivery; demos use synthetic pages only and need host-side controls for real use
Demos are macOS/Linux oriented for some kill experiments; live-model and vendor integrations (Muse, Grok, Codex) are marked not live-tested
Optional skill installer needs Node 22.20+; the README says the browser-only pages need no setup but the full demos need Node and Playwright
